summary: Log fire lookout from 1910, steel tower from 1919, closed by the mid-1950s and removed in 1977 or c.1985; the ridge lies in the Pepperbox Wilderness.

facts.design: steel tower with an enclosed cab (from 1919)
facts.status_note: Tower and observer's cabin removed; sources give 1977 or c.1985. No source describes the site today.

access.note: Pepperbox Wilderness, Forest Preserve land. No trail to the ridge; reaching it means off-trail navigation.

visit.trail_note: Trailhead on Moshier Road near the Beaver River. The trails are faint and obscure, and the tower site needs strong off-trail navigation.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: tower height (60 ft Aermotor for 1919 on the Forest Lookouts page, versus about 30 ft in the 1942 survey description quoted there) and removal date (1977 in two sources, c.1985 on the Forest Lookouts page). Probable duplicate: us-ny-beaver-lake-mountain-2 (Herkimer, Aermotor, 18.3 m, 'July 1910' in its agency field) describes this same tower, but its coordinates (41.08426, -74.58075) sit near the New Jersey border, far from Herkimer County; merge candidate. The record's point (43.91558, -75.13617) was not checked against a map; sources place the ridge north of Threemile Beaver Meadow, about four miles north of the village of Number Four.
